note: The diagnostic registry for SiteSkin Manifest 1.0. Machine-readable so the conformance corpus can assert that every code has at least one fixture and every fixture code is registered. A code with no fixture does not exist.

layers.transport: Enforced on the response before the body is parsed.
layers.parse: Enforced while turning bytes into JSON.
layers.version: Enforced on schemaVersion after parsing, before schema validation. Separate from 'schema' because siteskin-1.0.schema.json validates the version *format* only and does not pin the major, so an unsupported major is a policy rejection rather than a structural one.
layers.schema: Enforced by siteskin-1.0.schema.json. Structural validity only.
layers.security: Enforced by the security validator. Not expressible in JSON Schema — these rules depend on the serving origin, which the schema does not know.

dispositions.reject: The whole manifest is discarded and the browser stays in regular mode.
dispositions.drop-item: The offending element is removed; the rest of the manifest still applies.
dispositions.warn: Nothing is removed; the diagnostic is recorded for the developer inspector.

diagnostics.summary: Manifest body exceeds 128 KB. Enforced before parsing, so an oversized payload is never fully read into memory.
Response body is not valid JSON.
schemaVersion declares a major version this implementation does not understand. Silently reinterpreting an unknown format is how a security boundary becomes a guess.
Document fails siteskin-1.0.schema.json: a missing required field, a wrong type, or a malformed value. Absence of a required field is not an element that can be dropped, so this rejects.

A URL resolves outside the serving origin. Not expressible in JSON Schema, which does not know the origin the manifest was served from — this is the rule that makes the schema/security split necessary rather than tidy.

An asset URL lies outside the serving origin. Subdomains count as outside (ADR-004): a subdomain is frequently delegated to a third party, and inheriting the parent's branding would let that party impersonate it. The logo falls back to a monogram.

A field not defined in this schema version was ignored. Minor versions are additive, so unknown fields must never be fatal — this is the policy that lets a 1.1 manifest be served safely to a 1.0 reader. toolbar.showDomain reaches this path by design (ADR-006): it is ignored, not honoured.
